b01.evidence: The double underline is two independent strokes. The first argument is compressed into a joined low double-bowl/oval form against its parenthesis and still admits 0 or omega; the right-hand 0 is a separate closed oval. Do not discard the existing doubt on the strength of the blind 0 alone.

b02.evidence: The whole display was inspected. One left brace covers map, satisfait and the two equalities. All stars, dots, indices and ie. agree; the connector has a horizontal shaft and one downward terminal return, without a separately resolved upper wing. Retain its dash/arrow doubt. Display and brace serialization are not textual differences.

b03.evidence: The enlarged map shaft has one short downward terminal return and no resolved pointed head or second wing. The existing dash/arrow alternative remains; the source and target and étale agree.

b04.evidence: The D, low a/n/s bodies, tall looped l and low c/a/s ending support Dans le cas, but several joins coincide with the strike. The existing uncertainty is retained rather than declaring every letter certain.

b05.evidence: The two raised straight opening strokes and two closing strokes are present, with a separate comma. Backtick/apostrophe and straight-quote serializations represent the same handwritten quote pairs. The NB underline and starred object agree.

b06.evidence: The final part of singulière is tightly reduced: after the tall l and dotted i there is a low two-bend return, without a fully separable last e body. Singulière remains preferred, with the blind singulier now explicit as an alternative. Both raised quote pairs, following de, unstarred object and separate dotted object are clear.

b07.evidence: The opening and closing raised double marks around bord are distinct from the low final period. Their different TeX quote encodings do not change the ink.

b08.evidence: The upper-right glyph contains crossed strokes and more than one tiny internal light region, with a tall upper ray. This is a looped star like other superscripts on the page, rather than the single oval-and-tail construction of delta; it is also unlike the simple centered boundary dots. Retain the star.

b10.evidence: Both straight raised quote pairs and the complete Xi-star are present. Ouvertes has low opening strokes, a taller t and terminal e/s return. Quote serialization alone differs.

b11.evidence: The n has a raised little circle and the following numeral is 1. The degree-sign and superscript-o encodings represent the same ink. The outer opening parenthesis is real.

b12.evidence: The complete cancelled and replacement wording was inspected. The old forked first glyph, crossed X and covered relation remain uncertain. A tall old stroke and low ending still permit fermé; the blind et plus unreadable remainder is not sufficiently separable to replace it. The apparent low comma after old X joins the zigzag cancellation, so it is not certified as independent punctuation. The new opening parenthesis, Y subset X and inclusion lie on a higher baseline and are inserted; fermée continues on the original next baseline.

b13.evidence: Only one full-height right parenthesis and a lower comma follow fermée. The small oval between on and donc is visible. Both complete identities agree. Deux and loc. cit in the blind reading are neighboring lines already transcribed and are not duplicated.

b15.evidence: The broad bowl, high closed right loop and long return establish the script V alphabet. The first subscript is retraced and remains unsure Y; comma, X and final point are separate. Bracing and period inside or outside math delimiters do not change text.

b17.evidence: The final line has y avait lieu d-introduire followed by the same script symbol and point inspected in b15. The upper comme dans is adjacent context already present. Apostrophe style and macro bracing are serialization differences.
